bio.summary: Smith has run for Boulder council four times and is now a mayoral candidate. Known as “The Grateful Fred,” he proposes a local income tax on high earners, which would require a change in state law.
bio.note: Source availability is narrower than for questionnaire respondents; silence is not a policy position. The city elections page lists “Fred Smith,” while the official campaign-finance list calls the ballot name “Grateful Fred Instead” and records legal name Michael Smith: https://webapps.bouldercolorado.gov/election/report.php?electionID=25&report=candidateList .

statements.text: Fred wants Kinetics back at the Boulder Reservoir on the first Saturday in May.

statements.text: Smith fiercely opposed the TABOR Act and described how progressive taxes could strengthen the city.

statements.text: Students deserve a real voice in how Boulder raises and spends money, not a seat at the table after the decisions are made.
statements.speaker: Fred Smith

statements.text: Fred's proposal is a 10% city tax on household income above $184,500.
statements.speaker: Fred Smith campaign

statements.text: Smith proposes a 10% city income tax on household income above $184,500, which he estimates would generate $185 million annually. Because TABOR prohibits Colorado municipalities from imposing income taxes, Smith proposes pursuing a statewide ballot measure to authorize such taxes. He proposes using the revenue for public facilities, childcare, affordable housing and mental health care.
statements.speaker: Boulder Reporting Lab reporter
